abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made it exceptionally convenient for users to send their private data to model providers, which process them in plaintext. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) promises to secure remote inference by computing directly on encrypted data, yet it has remained prohibitively slow. The effort to make it practical remains fragmented, with most existing frameworks being closed-source, which keeps progress from compounding. We present Perseus, a free and open Python software library that supports the full stack of encrypted model inference, from the cryptographic backend and data packing, to encrypted nonlinearities and end-to-end model execution. Perseus ships with built-in novel optimizations, one at each level of the stack: in-kernel regeneration of key-switching keys at the (i) backend level, a complex variant of Cachemir packing at the (ii) data level, and a state-of-the-art bootstrap placer that is both packing- and magnitude-aware at the (iii) model level. Perseus achieves state-of-the-art latency across multiple models and modalities, within $3\%$ of the plaintext models' accuracy and perplexity. Remarkably, it is $3.96\times$ faster at single-token decoding than any other implementation on Llama-3-8B. We initiate, for the first time, a public speedrun on encrypted GPT-2, so that progress can compound.

sections.body: The section motivates the work: FHE inference is slow, and most optimizations sit in closed-source frameworks that do not integrate. The authors present Perseus, a Python library built on Perseus-core, a Rust and CUDA CKKS backend for 32-bit arithmetic and bootstrapping. Three built-in optimizations are listed: in-kernel regeneration of key-switching keys using `ChaCha12` (halving key storage), a complex variant of Cachemir packing (roughly halving memory), and bootstrap planning with an iterated minimum cut (approximately 30% fewer bootstraps). The section also announces a public leaderboard for encrypted GPT-2. Competing results are published numbers where code is unavailable, and reproduced numbers where it is available.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Perseus is a free open Python library that adds optimizations at every level of encrypted model inference.

sections.body: The authors split encrypted inference into three levels: the cryptographic backend, the data packing, and bootstrap placement. At the backend, half of each key-switching key is regenerated from a seed with a counter-mode ChaCha12 expander inside the two kernels that use it, which halves key storage. At the data level, Cachemir packing is extended from real to complex slots, carrying two real vectors per ciphertext, which roughly doubles throughput of many operations and roughly halves memory. At the model level, the placer uses each ciphertext's coefficient magnitude and packing periodicity in an iterated minimum cut. On average it runs approximately 30% fewer bootstraps than comparable placers.
sections.heading: Perseus
sections.headline: Perseus adds one optimization per stack level: key regeneration, complex-Cachemir packing, and a magnitude-aware bootstrap placer.

sections.body: All measurements use one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 with a 32-bit RNS CKKS chain at log N=16 and 128-bit security. Four models are tested: Llama-3-8B, GPT-2-small, ViT-B/16, and BERT-base, in prefill or decoding modes. For Llama-3-8B decoding, latency is 3.96 times lower than Sylph on HEaaN, with encrypted perplexity 7.77 against plaintext 7.76 at 512 context. GPT-2 decoding reaches perplexity 26.46 against 26.47 in plaintext, and prefill reaches normalized accuracy of 100% over 64 prompts. ViT reaches 96.9% and BERT 100% normalized accuracy. The authors also state that GPT-2 at 1.9 s/tok is a toy model meant as a development platform.
sections.heading: Results
sections.headline: Perseus reaches 3.96 times faster single-token decoding on Llama-3-8B and matches plaintext accuracy on the tested models.

sections.body: The authors place Perseus against GPU-oriented CKKS frameworks, several of which are closed-source, such as HEaaN. They note that Medha and REED halve key storage by regenerating keys from a seed, but only in custom hardware, whereas Perseus does this in-kernel on the GPU. They note that STIP and THEMIS use the imaginary half of the slots only in prefill, whereas complex-Cachemir extends this to decoding. For bootstrap placement, the authors state that existing placers decide from depth, latency, and scale, while theirs also reads coefficient magnitude and packing period for each ciphertext. Most prior LLM and encrypted-model systems improve only one stack level and release no code or only part of it.
sections.heading: Related Works
sections.headline: Prior work either regenerates keys only in custom hardware or uses the imaginary half of slots only during prefill.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the contributions: a publicly available Python library for encrypted model inference, lowest reported latency across multiple models and modalities at practically useful model sizes, and optimizations at key regeneration, complex-Cachemir, and magnitude-aware placement. The authors also present the public speedrun on encrypted GPT-2 as a shared workbench in which community optimizations can accumulate. The section does not add new measurements beyond those reported in the results.
sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.headline: Perseus delivers top latency across several models and modalities and opens a public GPT-2 speedrun.
